artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The pentagram map is a discrete dynamical system acting on projective equivalence classes of polygons in the projective plane: given a polygon P, one forms the new polygon T(P) whose vertices are the intersection points of consecutive shortest diagonals of P. Its 1‑dimensional analogue is the leapfrog map, a discrete map on configurations of points on the projective line defined using cross-ratios. The classical pentagram map and its higher-dimensional generalizations (acting on polygons in RP^d) are known to be completely integrable in the Liouville sense, with invariants constructed from a Lax representation and an underlying cluster/Poisson structure. A version of the pentagram map has also been defined for polygons in Grassmannians.

Problem. 
(a) Formulate a noncommutative analogue of the leapfrog map, in which the underlying scalar coordinates are replaced by elements of a noncommutative associative algebra (for example using a noncommutative cross-ratio), and establish its complete integrability in an appropriate noncommutative sense (e.g. existence of a sufficient family of commuting invariants with respect to a noncommutative Poisson/double-bracket structure, or a noncommutative Lax representation with a suitable spectral curve).

(b) Define noncommutative analogues of the pentagram map on polygons in the projective plane, of its higher-dimensional generalizations acting on polygons in higher projective spaces, and of the Grassmannian pentagram map (acting on polygons whose vertices lie in a Grassmannian). For each of these noncommutative maps, establish complete integrability in an appropriate noncommutative sense.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. The Grassmann pentagram map has been given a noncommutative interpretation (via Van den Bergh double brackets) and shown to be noncommutatively integrable (Izosimov, Adv. Math. 2020). A noncommutative leapfrog map was constructed and its integrability structure (Lax/zero-curvature representation, Poisson structure via noncommutative networks, and connection to noncommutative Laurent bi-orthogonal polynomials) was developed by Wang and collaborators (arXiv:2310.01993, J. London Math. Soc. 2025). However, a fully general noncommutative pentagram map in arbitrary dimensions with a complete proof of Liouville-type integrability is not yet established in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Non-commutative integrability of the Grassmann pentagram map
status_evidence.snippet: The Grassmann pentagram map is reinterpreted in terms of noncommutative algebra, in particular the double brackets of Van den Bergh, to establish a noncommutative version of integrability.
status_evidence.claim: Noncommutative integrability of the Grassmann pentagram map established.

status_evidence.title: On noncommutative leapfrog map (Wang, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit formula for the noncommutative leapfrog map and corresponding discrete zero-curvature equation; Poisson structure via noncommutative network.
status_evidence.claim: A noncommutative leapfrog map has been defined with Lax and Poisson structures.

status_evidence.title: On non-commutative leapfrog map (arXiv:2310.01993)
status_evidence.snippet: Noncommutative leapfrog map revisited from noncommutative Laurent bi-orthogonal polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Integrability structure of the noncommutative leapfrog map is studied.
